**MaxMart Retail - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript**

**Operator:**  
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the MaxMart Retail Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

**Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:**  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss MaxMart Retail's results for the Q2 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Emily Carter, Chief Merchandising Officer; Mike Rivera, Chief Stores Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Alex Thompson.

**Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:**  
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report MaxMart Retail's performance for the Q2 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Our brick-and-mortar network of over 1,200 stores remains resilient amid inflationary pressures, supply chain hurdles from Red Sea issues, and e-commerce now claiming 16.5% of U.S. retail sales according to Census Bureau figures. We're sharpening our omnichannel edge, fine-tuning our store fleet, and elevating customer experiences to grab share from online giants like Amazon and Wayfair while holding ground against Walmart and Home Depot.

On store fleet optimization and remodels, we're pushing forward with our NextGen Store program, now complete in 285 locations since early last year—beating our original goal. These updates bring open layouts, bigger zones for profitable areas like kitchen gear and furnishings, and RFID tech cutting shrink by 22 basis points per store. Remodeled spots posted 14.2% comp sales growth versus flat overall, with traffic rising 8% from app-based local promotions. In the Northeast, 65 New York and Boston stores drove 16% lifts in apparel amid a weak economy. Sunbelt wins include 12 small-format openings in Texas and Florida, hitting $1,200 sales per square foot—15% above big-box norms. We closed 18 Midwest underperformers and shifted 22 to BOPIS dark stores, trimming $45 million in SG&A.

Omnichannel sales hit 28% of revenue, up from 22%, with BOPIS up 35% to 1.2 million orders thanks to Scan & Go checkout in 400 stores slashing times by 40% and lifting baskets to $85. Our $150 million capex includes Shopify POS links and ShipBob micro-centers near 50 key stores. MaxMart Rewards reached 18 million members, up 24%, with AI personalization from Google Cloud boosting repeat visits 9%; digital comps soared 42%.

Supply chain sharpened too, with turns at 5.8x versus 5.2x, inventory down 8% to $2.1 billion via markdown control and vendor scorecards hitting 96% on-time delivery. Domestic apparel sourcing rose to 52%, dodging tariffs and freight spikes. Atlanta's automated DC handles 40% Southeast volume with Honeywell robotics, trimming costs 18% to $4.50 per order. VMI trials with P&G and Unilever aim for more margin gains.

Sustainability builds our edge: 25% drop in Scope 1/2 emissions via LEDs in 70% of stores and EV chargers at 300 sites—62% of shoppers favor green per our polls. Green Shelf private labels at 15% mix grew 28% with 200 bps margin boost; waste diversion hit 75% via Too Good To Go.

These moves compound: FY24 comps now guided to 3-5%, EBITDA margins to 7.2%. We're the community hub with cooking demos and such to fight showrooming. Risks like wage hikes and unemployment linger, but 55% gross margins and $800 million cash fuel M&A.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide more details on our financial results.

**Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:**  
Thank you, Alex. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q2 2024.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.8 billion, a 5.2% increase compared to the same period last year, powered by 4.2% comp store sales amid higher tickets in apparel and home goods.

Gross margin reached 38.5%, up a robust 230 basis points year-over-year from 36.2%—our best expansion in five years, beating Home Depot and Lowe's, thanks to our margin resilience push since FY22. Gross margin dollars climbed 7.2% to $2.8 billion alongside top-line growth and tight COGS control despite macro headwinds. Key drivers included a 510 basis point mix shift to high-margin pros at 45%+ now 32% of sales up from 28%, plus appliances at 42-48% riding housing renos. Lumber volumes rose 15% for Southeast rebuilds but only dinged margins 80 bps lapping shortages. SKU cuts of 18% since Q1 '23 slashed markdowns 25% and shrink to 1.2%. Freight normalized to $2,800 per FEU from peaks, a 150 bps boost via direct Asia containers at 65%; locked supplier deals offset steel/PVC inflation. Private labels at 28% of sales, up 400 bps, yield 52% margins via Carolinas manufacturing. Sunbelt margins up 320 bps to 40.1% on 8% Pro/outdoor comps; Northeast +190 bps to 37.8% with BOPIS turns at 5.8x; Midwest +120 bps to 36.9% despite lumber softness, aided by pricing AI versus Menards. Brick-to-Click investments like RFID in 1,200 stores hit 98.5% accuracy, cutting stockouts 30%. Q3 outlook 38.7-39.1%, full-year 180-200 bps expansion barring tariffs; Mexico nearshoring at 22% helps.

Operating expenses came in at $950 million, representing 38% of revenue, with standout labor discipline aiding control. Turning to store operations and payroll leverage—a profitability cornerstone in brick-and-mortar—we tracked it tightly across 1,200+ locations via sales per labor hour, countering wage inflation, turnover, and traffic shifts. Q2 brought 70 bps leverage to 10.1% of sales from 10.8%, sixth straight quarter improving, adding 40 bps to merchandise gross margin; two-year stack 150 bps. Comps at 4.2% let us flex labor smartly. Productivity surged: SPLH up 6.1% to $142, best since Q4 2021, via UKG Pro AI scheduling using store sensors and app data, cutting overstaffing 12%; supercenters hit 8% gains, grocery curbside +15%. Wages rose 4.2% to $17.85 matching industry, offset by incentives; turnover fell to 28% from 35% beating NRF's 32%, via Stay & Thrive with skills pay and Guild tuition—saving $18 million on training. Southeast/Midwest (55% square footage) leveraged 90 bps, SPLH +7.5% on low turnover and back-to-school; coastal California/Northeast (20%) +40 bps hit by min wages $16.50-$17, countered by self-checkout in 85% West stores trimming front-end labor 20%. Investments: $45 million in omnichannel hubs at 150 stores for BOPIS (22% sales, +10-15% SPLH), RFID pilots in 50 apparel stores cutting shrink labor 25%. Associate NPS up 12 to 82. Q3 leverage 50-60 bps on 3-4% comps, full-year $120-140 million savings for 75 bps op margin growth.

Net income stood at $120 million, or $0.85 per share. We generated $250 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently optimal, down 8% to $2.1 billion with turns at 5.8x from 5.2x, reflecting markdown discipline and vendor discipline.

Let me expand on our inventory optimization strategies, vital amid inflation, soft discretionary demand, and supply echoes at Target/Macy's. Brick-and-mortar drives 68% of our revenue. DIO fell from 62 to under 50 days versus 45-50 target; inventory -22% YoY to $1.1 billion, GMROI to 2.9x from 2.1x, shrink -15% to 1.2%. Pillars: AI forecasting via OptiPredict with IBM/Snowflake, Verkada sensors, weather/macro data—accuracy 92% from 78%, stockouts -35%, capturing $45 million in Sunbelt heatwave sales. Agile replen: 12 micro-fulfillment centers ($150M) with Locus/Symbotic cut leads to 24-48 hours for 70% SKUs; Southeast MFCs enable same-day for storms, safety stock -28%, 98% in-stock; Oakland offsets port delays. SKU prune to 38,000 from 45,000 via ABC-XYZ, localized planograms (Nielsen/Shelfgram)—markdowns -12% to 8.5%; Northeast privates 42%, Midwest durables. VMI with 60% top vendors like P&G/Stanley via SAP Ariba cuts costs 18%/$22M quarterly; Whirlpool real-time. Southeast/Midwest 6.4x turns; West 5.1x despite freight +9%. Canada aligns at 50 DIO. Ahead: RFID 200 stores -20% shrink, 20 MFCs, 6.5x turns—freed $180M working capital funds 12% dividend rise.

Regional performance showed clear variations across our 1,200 stores. National comps 3.8%, traffic +1.2%, conversion 28.5%, basket $112 +2.4%. Northeast (22% stores, 20% sales) -1.5% comps improving from Q1's -3.2%, traffic -4.1% from winter/urban rates sensitivity; margins 38.2%, shrink +20bps to 1.8%, turns 4.2x; loyalty 62% lifted bedding 12%. Midwest (28% stores, 30% sales) +0.1%, traffic +0.5%, kitchen/patio +2.1%; margins +80bps to 39.5% RFID shrink -15%, AUR +1.8%; rural +3% ag tailwinds. Southeast (25% stores, 27% sales) +8.2%, traffic +6.7%, basket $118 +4.5%, outdoor +15%; 12 new exurb stores +25% profitability, margins +120bps to 40.8% AI planograms -22% OOS. West (25% stores, 23% sales) +5.1%, PNW +7% home office +18%, CA +1.2% labor hit; BOPIS 18% up from 14%, turns 5.1x VMI. Sunbelt household growth vs. Northeast vacancies; outpace Macy's via local merch. Capex $150M: 50 Northeast express, 20 Southeast builds, StoreOS platform. Q3 comps 4-6%, Southeast 9-11%.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Emily Carter, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, followed by Mike Rivera to discuss store operations, and then Lisa Chen to discuss marketing initiatives.

**Emily Carter, Chief Merchandising Officer:**  
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we launched our EcoHome line, which has seen exceptional demand with 20% growth in sustainable home categories. We're excited about the potential of this new product and other upcoming launches.

**Mike Rivera, Chief Stores Officer:**  
Thank you, Emily. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. On footprint, Q2 saw 12 openings for FY24 total 58, mostly small-format 8,500 sq ft prototypes hitting $1,200/sq ft AUV versus $950 chain average—five Southeast in Atlanta/Nashville with BOPIS/design studios +15-20% ramp comps. Sunbelt added 28 doors on migration; Northeast closed eight urban under $700 AUV from remote work/office 18% vacancies. Total closures 22 Q2/82 FY, net -24 to 1,156 doors, 1.2% sq ft cut—1.8% churn below NRF 2.5%. Data-driven via Placer.ai/SafeGraph AI on SSS/EBITDA; Midwest 10 malls freed $45M for refreshes. Stores-as-hubs: 28% e-comm via BOPIS/ship-from, 42% digital blend. Pilots: three lifestyle centers Dallas/Phoenix/Denver +12% SSS. FY24: 45-50 opens/50-55 closes net flat, $120M capex 70% Sunbelt/Mtn West, small-formats to 20% by 2025, EV/drone features.

We've also ramped remodels: $450M FY24 capex up 25%, 40% budget. Pilots 150 stores +12.4% comps, dwell +28% to 42 min, conversion 22-31%, ticket $128 +15%, traffic +18% Placer.ai. Scale to 850/2,100 doors over 24 months, Phase1 400 at $1.2M/unit; costs -15% vendor deals. Essentials Hub: 2,000 sq ft kitchen anchors +40% appliances 45% margins, RFID shrink -22%, kiosks BOPIS 18-35%, demo kitchens Sub-Zero +24% kitchen comps. 60% recycled/LEED Silver, LEDs/HVAC +25% utility save $45K/store EBITDA $2.8M. Northeast 200 urban shrink checkouts, Midwest value pallets +16% basket, Sunbelt outdoor; Canada bilingual. 18-24 mo payback 15% IRR. Supply locks, in-house crews. Mirrors HD success, fortifies vs Amazon.

Positive results rolling in.

**Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer:**  
Thank you, Mike. Our new marketing campaign, MaxMart Rewards Boost, has increased brand awareness by 25%, driving deeper loyalty engagement.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

**Operator:**  
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

**John Smith (Goldman Sachs):**  
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your sales?

**Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:**  
Good morning, John. Inflation remains a headwind, with core CPI up 4.2%, but our value focus and private labels cushioned it. Comps hit 4.2% via higher-margin mix and Sunbelt strength, where household growth offset broader caution. Our pricing AI and localized assortments kept us competitive without erosion.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from Jane Roe with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

**Jane Roe (JPMorgan):**  
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

**Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:**  
Thanks, Jane. We're guiding Q3 comps to 4-6% nationally, led by Southeast at 9-11% on migration and seasonal prep, with Northeast stabilizing at 0-2%. This assumes steady consumer sentiment and our omnichannel momentum.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from Bob Wilson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

**Bob Wilson (Morgan Stanley):**  
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

**Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:**  
Absolutely, Bob. Inventory turns improved to 5.8x with 8% lower levels through AI forecasting at 92% accuracy, micro-fulfillment cutting leads to 24-48 hours, SKU rationalization down 16%, and VMI with top vendors saving $22 million quarterly. Atlanta DC robotics sped throughput 25%, domestic sourcing to 52% dodged freight hikes—setting us up strong.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from Alice Johnson with Barclays. Please go ahead.

**Alice Johnson (Barclays):**  
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

**Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:**  
Great question, Alice. MaxMart Rewards at 18 million members up 24% drove 9% repeat lifts via AI personalization, 28% omnichannel share, and 68% penetration in Southeast doubling repeats. It's fueling BOPIS surges and 42% digital comps, much like Target's playbook.

**Operator:**  
[Operator Instructions] That concludes today's questions.

**Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:**  
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

**Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:**  
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
